questions.q: What's the core difference between a For Loop container and a Foreach Loop container?
options: For Loop repeats based on an evaluated condition; Foreach Loop repeats once per item in a collection
For Loop can only run once; Foreach Loop can run unlimited times
For Loop requires a connection manager; Foreach Loop never does
There is no real difference — they're interchangeable
questions.explain: A For Loop container evaluates an expression each pass and stops when it's false; a Foreach Loop container runs once for every member of a specified enumerator's collection.

questions.q: Which For Loop expression is required, while the other two are optional?
options: EvalExpression
InitExpression
AssignExpression
All three are required
questions.explain: EvalExpression must be provided — it's what the loop checks each pass to decide whether to stop. InitExpression and AssignExpression are both optional.

questions.q: Which Foreach Loop enumerator would you use to process every file in a folder?
options: Foreach File Enumerator
Foreach ADO Enumerator
Foreach Nodelist Enumerator
Foreach SMO Enumerator
questions.explain: The Foreach File Enumerator is built specifically to enumerate files in a folder, optionally traversing subfolders.

questions.q: How many enumerator types can a single Foreach Loop container use at once?
options: Exactly one
As many as needed, mixed together
Two — a primary and a fallback
Zero — the enumerator is optional
questions.explain: A Foreach Loop container is configured with exactly one enumerator type. Looping over two different kinds of things requires two separate containers.

questions.q: What does the Foreach Loop's Variable Mappings page actually do?
options: Writes the enumerator's current value into a variable on every pass of the loop
Maps the loop's tasks to specific CPU cores
Defines which connection manager the enumerator uses
Sets the number of times the loop will repeat
questions.explain: Variable Mappings updates a chosen variable with the enumerator's current collection value each time the loop repeats, making that value available to the rest of the control flow.
